channel.title: Cybersecurity News
channel.description: Notable but non-breaking cybersecurity news, one finding per item: short summary plus link to the original story.

item.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup (ex-SkyKick) app credential stolen and used to access Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress confirms 173
item.description:
Attackers got hold of the Microsoft 365 app credential behind ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick), a backup service MSPs install with broad access to mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams and directory data. On Oct 15 they scripted Microsoft Graph token grabs across tenants from 144.172.64[.]128, and Huntress has confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 173 partner and customer tenants. In at least one tenant a separate ConnectWise Teams app gave itself Global Administrator and added credentials to other trusted apps.

ConnectWise has shut down application access for the service, and Microsoft confirmed the activity. Anyone with the app consented should review service principal sign-ins, OAuth grants and app credentials now.

Sources: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News

item.title: ETS hack exposes data on about 7 million California public school students
item.description:
Educational Testing Service, California's statewide testing contractor, says an attacker used a compromised login to copy files from its SFTP site between May 22 and Sept 18, 2026. The data covers all students enrolled in the past three school years, roughly 7 million, including names, birth dates, addresses, disability status, program eligibility and test results. ETS found the activity Sept 25 and began notifying families Oct 16 with two years of Experian identity protection; no SSNs or financial data were involved.

Sources: Los Angeles Times, Politico, California Department of Education notice

item.title: Florida DMV breach exposed driver license and vehicle records, including document images, statewide
item.description:
Florida's Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) disclosed on October 16 that an international cybercriminal group got into its driver and vehicle database on September 4 using credentials a Plant City Police Department employee had stored on a personal device. Driver license and motor vehicle data, document images, and other personal information may have been accessed.

The agency says it contained the access and has seen no misuse, but it has not said how many people are affected. Florida Politics reports the attackers set a September 11 deadline to make a deal before leaking the data. Letters are going out to current license and ID holders with a year of free credit monitoring.

Sources: Boca Post, Florida Politics, FLHSMV notice

item.title: Max-severity BlockStrap flaw in Magento and Adobe Commerce lets attackers run PHP code; Sansec expects mass exploitation soon
item.description:
CVE-2026-103849, dubbed BlockStrap, is a template-engine injection in Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce (through 2.4.9, and B2B through 1.5.3) that lets attacker-controlled email template content execute arbitrary PHP code on store servers. Adobe patched it on October 13 but rated it priority 2.

Sansec says no attacks have been seen yet, but it found four possible attack paths in under a day and expects mass exploitation soon, noting the similar StyleSmuggler flaw went from hotfix to mass attacks in three days. Stores need the October release or Adobe's isolated patch, and should keep the September StyleSmuggler hotfix in place too. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Attackers tampered with AOMEI Backupper update servers to push a backdoor to Windows machines
item.description:
Between May and July 2026, attackers repeatedly altered the update and notification config files on AOMEI's own servers for five-to-ten-minute windows, so any AOMEI Backupper install that checked in during a window downloaded and ran a backdoor. Google Threat Intelligence Group, Mandiant and ManageEngine's Threat Analysis Lab disclosed the campaign this week.

The software never cryptographically verified those files, and the checksum sat inside the same unsigned file. AOMEI says its servers are fixed, but that does not clean machines already hit. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: CISA adds BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day and Fortinet PEERSTITCH-linked flaw to KEV with Oct 19 deadline
item.description:
CISA added two exploited flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 16: BeyondTrust Remote Support auth bypass CVE-2026-102764 (BT26-05, exploited by China-nexus actors since August) and Fortinet path traversal CVE-2025-61624 in FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy and FortiSwitchManager, which surfaced in the PEERSTITCH FortiGate implant campaign.

Both carry a short Oct 19 remediation deadline and CISA's forensic triage requirement. Sources: CISA alert, BeyondTrust BT26-05, Fortinet FG-IR-26-122

item.title: Juniper patches 150+ Junos OS flaws, about two dozen critical; F5 fixes 11 NGINX bugs
item.description:
Juniper Networks published 17 advisories covering more than 150 vulnerabilities in Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved, plus four in Juniper Cloud-Native Router. Roughly two dozen are rated critical and can lead to code or command execution as root, full device takeover, kernel panics, or Routing Engine reboots.

F5 separately fixed 11 NGINX flaws, including critical unauthenticated bugs CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479 and CVE-2026-97205 that can crash workers or reach RCE if ASLR is disabled or bypassed. Neither vendor reports in-the-wild exploitation. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Burger King Japan breach exposes about 11.18 million app member records
item.description:
Burger King Japan said a follow-up investigation concluded Oct 13 found unauthorized access between Oct 2 and Oct 7 to the server holding official smartphone-app member data, exposing about 11.18 million customer records. Stolen fields include names, dates of birth, gender, email addresses, phone numbers, and order history; the company says the server did not store credit card numbers and it found no evidence that user credentials were accessed.

Access from the suspicious source was blocked after discovery, the breach was reported to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission, and no secondary fraudulent use has been confirmed so far. Customers were warned to watch for phishing that impersonates BK Japan. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Unit 42 details PEERSTITCH FortiGate implant after FortiManager breach hit 500+ firewalls
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 disclosed PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 FortiGate implant used in a September 2024 intrusion (CL-STA-0954 / UNC5820) against a telecommunications MSP. Attackers first exploited FortiJump (CVE-2024-47575) on FortiManager, exfiltrating configs, crypto material, and data covering more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls, then used FortiOS CLI path-traversal CVE-2025-61624 to escalate to root and inject the implant into miglogd and iked.

PEERSTITCH leaves no disk binary, opens no listening ports, and builds a covert inter-process bridge so tagged VPN sessions can bypass FortiOS security checks—hard for conventional EDR/network tools to see. FortiJump and the path-traversal flaw are already patched; defenders should hunt edge appliances for auto-script traversal artifacts, rotate FortiManager-held credentials and keys, and review Unit 42 IOCs. Not a new mass internet zero-day today, but a significant edge-malware disclosure.

Sources: unit42.paloaltonetworks.com; thehackernews.com

item.title: Central Ohio Primary Care breach hits about 1.4 million after August vishing attack
item.description:
Central Ohio Primary Care (COPC) said on Oct 15 that a cybersecurity incident discovered Aug 25, stemming from a social-engineering vishing attack aimed at extortion, may have exposed personal and protected health information for about 1.4 million patients and employees. Potentially affected data can include names, addresses, Social Security numbers, limited patient health data, financial information, and other identifiers; MyChart/Epic was not impacted and COPC says the incident is contained with no known misuse so far.

COPC is notifying affected people, offering credit and dark-web monitoring, and working with law enforcement. Local reporting has tied the intrusion to ransomware activity, but COPC's public statement focuses on the vishing entry and file access rather than naming a group. Sources: copcp.com; 10tv.com

item.title: BAE Systems cyber incident disrupts nationwide Bankruptcy Noticing Center
item.description:
The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts said a cybersecurity incident affecting BAE Systems IT and websites that support the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has halted production and delivery of electronic and paper bankruptcy notices for federal bankruptcy courts nationwide. BAE operates BNC systems on behalf of the judiciary; related sites including bnc.uscourts.gov, bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov, notices.uscourts.gov, and the National Creditor Registration Service are unavailable while BAE investigates and works to restore service.

CM/ECF Notices of Electronic Filing continue to work, and courts are still accepting filings, but creditor noticing and mailing-label access are disrupted; the outage has been ongoing since about Oct 9. Source: uscourts.gov

item.title: China-nexus ARMORY CASTLE exploited BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day CVE-2026-102764 (BT26-05)
item.description:
BeyondTrust and Mandiant/GTIG disclosed CVE-2026-102764 (BT26-05, CVSS 9.3), a critical Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) flaw that lets a remote attacker perform arbitrary file operations on an affected appliance. Mandiant says suspected China-nexus espionage actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221; CrowdStrike: WARP PANDA) exploited it as a zero-day in late August 2026, then planted the SAWFLY webshell, gained root, and targeted brokered credentials.

BeyondTrust reports confirmed exploitation of one BeyondTrust-hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance; SaaS was auto-patched October 8, and self-hosted Remote Support (and precautionarily Privileged Remote Access) customers must apply BT26-05 immediately. Technical exploit details are withheld while self-hosted fleets patch. Mandiant warns defenders should expect broader opportunistic scanning after disclosure. Not in CISA KEV as of this check.

Sources: cloud.google.com; beyondtrust.com; BeyondTrust advisories

item.title: Critical PwnEscape Linux kernel flaw lets guest VMs read host memory (CVE-2026-99999); confirmed on Vercel sandboxes
item.description:
Paulos Yibelo of pwn.ai disclosed CVE-2026-99999 (PwnEscape), a critical (CVSS 9.3) Linux kernel networking flaw where crafted packets from inside a guest VM can leak host memory (~32 bytes per packet), and in lab setups crash the host or escape to host admin control. Vercel confirmed the memory leak against its production Firecracker sandboxes during an August challenge; crash and code execution were demonstrated only on matching lab hosts, not as production RCE.

The bug sits in shared host networking code, not a Vercel-specific misconfig, so it matters for multi-tenant clouds that isolate workloads with Linux/KVM. Attack vector is local (attacker must already run code in a guest). No in-the-wild exploitation or KEV listing as of Oct 15. Patch host kernels to fixed stables (e.g. 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.57, 7.2.11) or your distro backport and reboot; guest-only updates do not help.

Sources: thehackernews.com; pwn.ai; vercel.com

item.title: CISA adds Atlassian pre-auth arbitrary file read across Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket and more to KEV (CVE-2026-21589)
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-21589 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 15, confirming in-the-wild exploitation of an unauthenticated file-access flaw in Atlassian Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye. It lets an attacker read specific files inside the web application root; watchTowr published technical details on Oct 6. CISA set a short Oct 18 deadline and flagged it for forensic triage, so patch self-hosted Atlassian instances per the vendor advisory and check for signs of access. Source: confluence.atlassian.com (KEV: cisa.gov)

item.title: Fake yay and paru AUR packages push malware that runs with root on Arch Linux
item.description: A user named marchos1as mass-uploaded typosquatted Arch User Repository packages (such as yyay) impersonating the popular yay and paru AUR helpers, detected Oct 13. The packages bundled legitimate upstream code with an install scriptlet that fetched and ran a remote shell script as root, pulled via a Wayback Machine URL pointing to a GitFlic repo tied to the earlier npm DirtyBlanket campaign. The AUR team banned the account and removed the packages; anyone who installed a misspelled yay/paru package should treat the host as compromised. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: GhostAction GitHub supply-chain campaign hijacks about 1,900 accounts, targets 30,000+ repositories
item.description: GitGuardian says the GhostAction credential-theft campaign spiked on Oct 8-9, compromising about 1,900 GitHub accounts and targeting more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and orgs, attempting to pull 3,174 secrets from CI. Attackers use stolen PATs or infostealer credentials to push malicious workflows disguised as security-audit.yml or github_actions_security.yml that exfiltrate CI/CD, cloud, npm/PyPI/Docker Hub and AI API secrets, with newer payloads also scanning git history. Review recent workflow additions and rotate any CI secrets exposed in affected repos. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: NGINX fixes five flaws, including possible RCE memory bugs and a TLS client-cert bypass
item.description: NGINX 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 (Oct 14) fix five bugs, one present in every release since 2005. Three memory bugs (F5 CVSS v4 9.2) could crash workers or possibly allow code execution, and a session-ticket key rotation bug can let a forged TLS session bypass client-certificate checks when the common shared session cache is used. Each needs a specific config (alias with rewrite, regex map, AIO with SSI, shared TLS session cache, or HTTP/3); no exploitation or KEV listing as of Oct 15. Upgrade NGINX or apply F5's workarounds. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: UK Legal Aid Agency breach scope widens: stolen records date back to 1978
item.description: The UK Ministry of Justice's Legal Aid Agency says a forensic review shows attackers who breached its systems in April 2025 stole records going back to 1978, far earlier than the 2010-onward data it previously confirmed. Stolen applicant data includes contact details, dates of birth, national ID numbers, criminal history, employment status and financial details, plus legal aid provider data. The update materially widens one of the UK government's most sensitive breaches. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Next.js ships out-of-band patches for two critical unauthenticated RCE flaws (CVE-2026-96889)
item.description: Next.js released 16.4.1 and 15.5.28 on Oct 14 to fix two critical unauthenticated remote code execution bugs (Vercel CVSS 9.5 each) plus a high-severity Server Actions DoS. One sits in React Server Components `use cache` (GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr) when Cache Components return multiple typed arrays; the other is librsvg CVE-2026-96889 reachable via sharp SVG handling on glibc Linux (and next/og). No in-the-wild exploitation reported as of Oct 15. Upgrade Next.js, confirm sharp is 0.35.5+, then rebuild and redeploy. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: Drupal patches critical Field UI flaw with unauthenticated RCE path via contributed modules (CVE-2026-108097)
item.description: Drupal shipped critical fixes in 11.4.10, 11.3.19, and 10.6.19 on Oct 14 for CVE-2026-108097 in Field UI: a render-callback abuse that can lead to remote code execution. Core alone is not enough to reach it, but several contributed-module paths exist and at least one needs no login. About 28.5% of reporting sites were on affected branches in early October; no public exploit or attacks reported yet. Update ASAP or temporarily uninstall field_ui; Entity List module CVE-2026-108099 needs its own 3.0.10 update. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: CenterPoint Energy breach hits 1.06 million Texans with SSNs and driver's licenses
item.description: Houston utility CenterPoint Energy told the Texas Attorney General that 1,062,060 state residents had names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and driver's license numbers compromised. The notice follows a September SEC filing after a threat actor posted a claim of ~7.5 million records and a 2.5 GB dump. Operations were not disrupted; impact in Indiana, Minnesota, and Ohio is still unclear, and customer notification letters may not have gone out yet. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Langflow authenticated RCE CVE-2026-105740 hit with 1,423 honeypot exploit attempts
item.description: Previdian reports 1,423 exploitation attempts since Sep 19 against Langflow CVE-2026-105740 (CVSS 9.9), an authenticated RCE where any logged-in user can inject OS commands via MCP stdio server config (bash -c with no validation). Attackers brute-force or use weak creds, then steal LANGFLOW_SECRET_KEY and related secrets; activity spiked Oct 11 and continues Oct 15. Patch to 1.9.0+, disable auto-login, enforce strong passwords, and review /api/v2/mcp/servers/ logs. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: Claude Code Desktop "SneakPeek" preview-pane flaw let poisoned repos silently steal developer secrets (patched)
item.description: Noma Labs disclosed SneakPeek (CVSS 8.7), a zero-click chain in Anthropic's Claude Code Desktop preview pane: HTML files over 256KB were loaded as file:// URLs with no CSP and no active request filter, so a poisoned file in a public repo could run JavaScript and exfiltrate SSH keys, AWS/GitHub credentials, API keys and Claude OAuth tokens when a developer asked Claude to review it. Anthropic's first fix (July 9) was bypassed via a blob: Web Worker; the full fix shipped Aug 17 in Claude Desktop 1.30096.1 and later. No in-the-wild exploitation reported; make sure Claude Desktop is current and keep long-lived credentials off dev machines. Sources: noma.security ; darkreading.com

item.title: CISA adds Palo Alto PAN-OS authenticated management RCE to KEV (CVE-2026-0322)
item.description: CISA's KEV catalog moved to version 2026.10.14 (count 1745) and added CVE-2026-0322, a code-injection bug in the Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management web UI that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama. Palo Alto rates urgency Highest, says very limited exploitation has been seen, and lists IoCs 66.42.72.14, 208.83.239.114, and 149.248.47.234. Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access are not affected; patch to the listed fixed builds and keep management off the public internet. Sources: security.paloaltonetworks.com ; cisa.gov

item.title: CISA adds AhsayCBS auth-bypass + unauth RCE chain to KEV (CVE-2026-105133 / CVE-2026-105134)
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-105133 (improper authentication) and CVE-2026-105134 (command injection) in AhsayCBS backup consoles to KEV on Oct 14, with a federal due date of Oct 17. Huntress saw the chain exploited from Oct 7 for unauthenticated SYSTEM RCE, JSP webshells, and XMRig miners disguised as Edge across at least five organizations; Ahsay's earlier 10.3.4.0 / 9.15.2.59 builds did not fully fix it. Apply hotfixes 10.3.4.45 (v10) or 9.15.2.70 (v7–v9), reboot, and treat exposed management interfaces as compromised until verified. Sources: huntress.com ; ahsay.com

item.title: CISA adds Cisco Secure Email Gateway exploited zero-day CVE-2026-76519 to KEV
item.description: Material update: CISA listed CVE-2026-76519 in KEV on Oct 14 (catalog 2026.10.14), with remediation due Oct 17 and forensic triage required. Cisco disclosed the CVSS 9.8 relative path traversal the same day as an actively exploited arbitrary file write via AMP File Reputation attachments on Secure Email Gateway; only gateways with File Reputation on and Content Scanner Tools older than 25.3.0.5525 are affected. Update Content Scanner Tools or move to AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 / 16.5.0-780 and hunt system_logs for compromise indicators. Sources: sec.cloudapps.cisco.com ; cisa.gov

item.title: Hackers backdoor Nextcloud servers via Collabora Built-in CODE app (CVE-2026-110447)
item.description: Attackers exploited an unauthenticated OS command injection in Nextcloud's optional Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) before 26.4.303, planting PHP webshells (shx*.php) when the local CODE server was down. Collabora published CVE-2026-110447 on Oct 14 with evidence of in-the-wild exploitation since September; disabling the app is not enough—update to 26.4.303+ or remove it. Standalone Collabora Online and Docker/package CODE setups are not affected. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens 17 advisories; Rockwell ArmorBlock critical takeover flaw
item.description: Siemens issued 17 ICS advisories this Patch Tuesday, including critical issues in Simatic S7-1500 CPUs, Industrial Edge, and Ruggedcom Crossbow SAC. Rockwell fixed a critical unauthenticated ArmorBlock web-server password change that can lead to admin takeover, plus a DoS. Schneider published two high-severity advisories; CISA also posted ICS notes on Swann cameras and Inductive Automation Ignition. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Cisco patches second exploited Secure Email Gateway zero-day giving unauthenticated root (CVE-2026-76519)
item.description: On Oct 14 Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8), an arbitrary file write in the AMP File Reputation feature of Secure Email Gateway. A crafted email attachment lets an unauthenticated remote attacker write files and run commands as root. Cisco says it learned of active exploitation this month. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled and Content Scanner Tools older than 25.3.0.5525 are affected, and there is no workaround. Update Content Scanner Tools or move to AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 or 16.5.0-780, then check system_logs for "System Security" compromise indicators. This is the second exploited SEG zero-day in a month, after CVE-2026-76461 in September. Sources: sec.cloudapps.cisco.com ; bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: CISA urges immediate Ivanti Connect Secure patching as exploit attempts spread (CVE-2026-104935)
item.description: CISA put out an advisory telling all organizations, not just federal agencies, to update Ivanti Connect Secure right away and run network and memory forensics, because Ivanti's Integrity Checker may miss in-memory attacks. Previdian honeypots logged 105 exploit attempts from 50 IPs as of Oct 14. So far they're mostly tests for code execution, and watchTowr expects mass exploitation to follow. Shadowserver tracks about 5,600 internet-exposed ICS hosts. A fix for the third bug in the chain, the privilege escalation, is still pending. Sources: thehackernews.com ; bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Microsoft and Health-ISAC disrupt Chinese-language phishing kits behind 1B+ messages
item.description: With a federal court order, Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, Health-ISAC, Japan's JC3 and partners including Cloudflare, Proofpoint and Resecurity seized domains behind the CoGUI, Haozi and Iron Man System phishing kits. The kits are tied to the YAM Store marketplace and initial access broker. Since January 2026 they have helped send more than a billion phishing emails and SMS messages to over 75,000 organizations in about 150 countries. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: US shuts down 40+ laptop farms and charges 14 in North Korean IT worker scheme
item.description: The DOJ charged 14 people, a mix of US citizens and Chinese nationals, and seized about 187 computers in raids on more than 40 laptop farms. The farms let North Korean IT workers pose as US-based remote hires. The scheme reached more than 70 US companies and stole the identities of at least 25 Americans. Two Americans were arrested. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: curl 8.23.0 fixes High-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free with code-execution PoC (CVE-2026-92392)
item.description: A use-after-free in curl/libcurl 8.12.0 through 8.22.0 lets a malicious HTTPS server that receives a roughly 135KB HTTP/2 upload corrupt client memory. The reporter's public PoC turns that into code execution. It's curl's first High-severity bug since October 2023, and Anthropic's OSS Scanner found it. curl says a real-world attack would most likely just cause a crash, and no exploitation is reported. Upgrade to 8.23.0 or a fixed branch release (8.14.3, 8.16.2, 8.20.2), or force HTTP/1.1 until you can. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: Fortinet fixes critical unauthenticated RCE and auth bypass in FortiSIEM and FortiSandbox
item.description: Fortinet's October advisories fix 13 bugs. Two are critical: an unauthenticated code execution flaw (CVE-2026-106173) and an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656) in FortiSIEM and the FortiSandbox GUI. There are also five high-severity authenticated SQL or command injection bugs across FortiAnalyzer, FortiManager and FortiMail. The same Patch Tuesday round includes Citrix XenServer/Workspace fixes and critical Ivanti Neurons Patch for Intune and Xtraction bugs. No exploitation is mentioned. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Vghost Linux kernel vhost flaw gives local root and VM-to-host escape (CVE-2026-74580)
item.description: Tencent Zhuque Lab published working demos of CVE-2026-74580 (Vghost), a vhost subsystem bug present across nearly a decade of Linux kernels. It gives an unprivileged local user reliable kernel read/write and root, and in one virtualization setup it lets an untrusted guest VM write to host memory and hijack the VM process. A fix went upstream on Aug 3, and there's no public sign of exploitation. Check that hosts exposing /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock run patched kernels. Source: thehackernews.com

item.title: Ledger signers sold via CryptoBilis reseller carried hardware implant tied to $86M crypto theft
item.description: Ledger confirmed on Oct 13 that all confirmed fund losses in its recent theft incident involved signers sold through Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis. Someone in the distribution chain soldered a small implant inside the devices that reads the 24-word recovery phrase off the screen during setup and sends it out over LTE using an eSIM. On-chain investigator Specter puts losses above $86 million, though Ledger hasn't confirmed a total, and it advises buyers from that reseller in the last 90 days to move funds to a new signer with a new seed. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Ahold Delhaize takes systems offline after cyberattack disrupting grocery brands
item.description: Dutch-Belgian grocery giant Ahold Delhaize disconnected some systems after detecting a security issue in its network. Local media report delivery and online-order disruption at Albert Heijn and Delhaize in Belgium and the Netherlands, and US stores appear affected too. The company says it has no evidence customer or employee data was stolen and is starting a controlled relaunch of systems. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: Meta notifies about 1,500 people after hackers accessed its GitHub repositories
item.description: An outside group used an employee's stolen credentials to access some of Meta's GitHub repositories, taking mostly product source code. About 1% of the stolen data was personal information, mostly of US employees, that had been committed to the repos against policy. Meta cut off access, brought in GitHub and law enforcement, and is offering credit and dark web monitoring. Source: securityweek.com

item.title: SAP patches CVSS 10 OAuth2 SSRF in Cloud SDK for Python (CVE-2026-89111)
item.description: SAP's October 2026 updates fix 20 flaws, led by a maximum-severity SSRF in the Cloud SDK for Python used for BTP apps and AI agents. An unauthenticated attacker who controls the tenant_subdomain parameter can redirect OAuth2 token requests and steal client credentials in multi-tenant apps; an allowlist on tenant_subdomain is the interim mitigation. SAP also fixed critical NetWeaver Visual Composer (CVE-2026-89110) and MII (CVE-2026-89108) bugs. No exploitation reported. Source: bleepingcomputer.com

item.title: Critical Ghostscript flaw CVE-2026-39919 enables RCE via crafted PDF uploads
item.description:
Wordfence disclosed a critical heap buffer overflow in Ghostscript 9.21 through 10.07.1 that can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution when a server renders an attacker-supplied PDF, for example WordPress thumbnail generation via Imagick and ImageMagick. Researchers built proof-of-concept exploits, though success depended heavily on the environment and was not reliable on stock Linux packages. Artifex fixed it in Ghostscript 10.08.0 on September 8, with backports for older versions; no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Microsoft October 2026 Patch Tuesday: record 1,411 flaws, exploited Windows Shell zero-day
item.description:
Microsoft's October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes a record 1,411 vulnerabilities, including 70 rated Critical and 317 remote code execution bugs. The one actively exploited zero-day, CVE-2026-96951, is a Windows Shell command-injection flaw that bypasses Mark of the Web protections; CISA added it to KEV with an October 16 deadline. Two other zero-days were publicly disclosed, and Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of support with this release.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: GitLab patches CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated code execution flaw (CVE-2026-97229)
item.description:
GitLab fixed a maximum-severity integer overflow in CE and EE that, under certain conditions, lets an unauthenticated user run arbitrary code on the server through a crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration. Affected versions are 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2. No exploitation has been reported yet, but last month's CVSS 10 GitLab bug drew in-the-wild probes within hours, so self-managed instances should patch quickly.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers push, pull or delete images as other users (CVE-2026-105445)
item.description:
Docker disclosed a critical Docker Hub bug, open from August 2024 until September 30, 2026, where converting a personal account into an organization silently transferred its access tokens to whichever user was named owner. An attacker could use this to push, pull or delete images in another user's repositories, a real container supply-chain risk. Docker fixed it server-side and says it found no evidence of exploitation; CVSS 4.0 score is 9.4.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain exploited for root; KEV add, one fix still pending
item.description:
Volexity found attacker UTA0576 chaining three Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days since October 3 to run commands as root without logging in, even on a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance. Ivanti fixed the authentication bypass and RCE pair (CVE-2026-104935) on October 13 and reports limited exploitation; CISA added it to KEV with an October 16 deadline. The privilege-escalation fix is still weeks away, and Ivanti's Integrity Checker misses this in-memory chain, so forensic review is needed to confirm compromise.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Attackers hijack Danfoss refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets
item.description:
On the night of October 11, attackers took remote control of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC store refrigeration controllers and forced fridges and freezers into defrost, heating them to as much as 50°C and spoiling food at hundreds of Intermarché, Netto and other stores. CERT-FR reported numerous compromises and told operators to disconnect the controllers or tightly filter access. Danfoss says most affected units were older models it no longer updates; the attacker and entry method are not yet known.

Source: The Hacker News
